newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire coalition opposes video gambling.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire coalition opposes video gambling.

text.p: Opponents and supporters of video gambling collided on Tuesday at the New Hampshire State House, as a coalition of clergy, physicians and law enforcement officials called on Gov. Jeanne Shaheen to drop proposed legislation to allow racetracks to install video slot machines.

"Wherever we have looked across the face of the United States of America, we have seen expanded gambling violate individuals, families and communities," said David Lamar- Vincent of the Granite State Coalition Against the Expansion of Gambling.

Other members of the coalition, which include the state Chiefs of Police Association, New Hampshire Medical Society and the Christian Coalition, said legalizing video gambling would create more gambling addicts and bring more organized crime to the state.

House and Senate lawmakers who backed several proposals to either study video gambling or allow racetracks and some hotels install machines, withdrew their legislation on Tuesday. Coalition spokesman Bruce Keough of Exeter said the sponsors bowed to concerns raised about video gambling and opposition by top House Republican lawmakers.
Keough advised Shaheen to drop any plans to introduce a video gambling bill, citing stronger opposition from the coalition and legislators.

During her election campaign, Shaheen, a Democrat, supported proposals for a limited number of video slot machines at Rockingham Park, a racetrack in Salem, and three greyhound racing venues in Seabrook, Hinsdale and Belmont.
Supporters of video gambling say 5,000 machines could raise as much as $45 million a year for the state treasury. Shaheen said gambling revenue could be used to fund public education.
Critics of the coalition, such as George Roberts, a lobbyist representing racetracks, said it was overlooking the state's 90-year love affair with gambling.
"We were the first state with a lottery, and we encouraged the racing industry. We have bingo, Monte Carlo nights and Powerball. This isn't any different," Roberts said.
